title: A cut's exit notes reach no log when the signal that ends it takes the tee and no person is at a terminal
body:
A cut's exit trap, run_exit in lib/cmd/release, writes two lines as the run ends: that the local gates were stopped, and which candidate the run pushed and never reached the delete of, with the command that deletes it. ST0011 WP02b-1 (CRITIC-2's D-W1) sends each line through run_exit_say:
- to stderr, where tee takes it into the RELEASE log;
- or, when that write fails because the signal that ended the run took the tee with it, to /dev/tty where a person is at a terminal.

What is left: a signal that takes the tee where no person is at a terminal leaves the line in no log and on no screen. A TERM to a CI job or a cancelled booking's job are such signals. The next cut of the release still deletes a candidate left that way, so the release is not at risk, but the record of why is missing.

Why it is not fixed in the cut: the run's log path is a local of run_gate in lib/runlog. The cut cannot append to the log by path without run_gate publishing that path, for the gate now running.

Fix: run_gate publishes the log path of the gate it runs, and run_exit_say appends its line there by path whenever the stderr write fails, as well as writing to the terminal where there is one. Add an arm with a candidate leg, a TERM to the cut's whole group while its local gates run, and the note asserted in the RELEASE log.

Order: after issue 0306, which is changing lib/runlog now. Owner: set when 0306 lands.


Also (CRITIC-4 on ST0011 WP02b-1, its R1): two lines can be written during the exit trap outside run_exit_say, legs_local_stop's line naming a process group that was never written and legs_local_running's line naming a job table that cannot be written, so a signal that took the tee loses them even where a person is at a terminal. They go through run_exit_say with the rest.

Resolution (cc, 2026-11-05 05:48Z by date -u): fixed at bc83f3ab1b94532b495057c223b58a019cf4428a, landed on main by devbin-vc's land-stack.sh from the tested tip 487f5243, its tree outside intent/ equal to it, unpushed until the 0.1.20 cut. run_gate (lib/runlog) now names the run's own log to what it runs, as DEVBIN_GATE_LOG, for that command alone; its shell catches the signal and seals only once the command has ended, so a line appended by path is in the log before the seal reads it. release_say (lib/release.steps) is run_exit_say moved beside the library's notices and renamed: it writes to stderr, and where that write fails, the signal having taken the tee, it appends the line to DEVBIN_GATE_LOG by path and shows it at the terminal where a person is at one. The cut's exit notes, its candidate note, and the two notices the issue's R1 names (release_run_stop's unwritten process group and release_job_running's unwritable job table) go through it. docs/configuration.md says where the notes go, and docs/authoring-commands.md lists DEVBIN_GATE_LOG. The arm, in releasecut.bats: a cut with a candidate leg, its gates sleeping, ended by a TERM to its whole group, tee included, leaves both notes in its RELEASE log, read once the whole group has gone. Its runs, under hv's rule that a fix runs its own arms alone (decision 138), on devbin-vc's desk: the first, in slot 01M6N37K25PA3GF4QX5073H1QY at 5b284976, was void, since the arm read the log as the job's leader died, before the cut's exit trap and the gate's seal had run, so its red at main and at the fix proved nothing; the arm then waited for the group to end, and the rerun, in slot 01M6N3R82M89AJ955ZD50T9GW0 at 487f5243 on cef4d77c, had the arm red at main's code with the unit's releasecut.bats on its own property (the log, read after the seal, held neither note) and, with the signal arm beside it, green at the tip under BSD, 2 ok of 2. No arm reaches the two R1 notices, which need a process group or a job table that cannot be written. The cut's own gates, kovacs leg and CI are the one full test.
